entry.label: Systems practice
entry.description: The situated use of systems ideas, methods and judgement to inquire and act in a problematic situation. It includes choosing boundaries, combining approaches, learning from consequences and allowing the inquiry to change the practitioner as well as the situation.

profile.title: Systems practice
profile.canonical_definition: The situated use of systems ideas, methods and judgement to inquire and act in a problematic situation. It includes choosing boundaries, combining approaches, learning from consequences and allowing the inquiry to change the practitioner as well as the situation.
profile.summary: Situated inquiry and action using systems concepts, approaches, models and intervention judgement. Professional practice includes choosing and combining approaches, working with stakeholders and power, testing consequences, learning and reflecting on the practitioner’s own participation.
profile.why_it_matters: Systems practice is wider than systems mapping and wider than any single methodology. The occupational standard and SCiO competence structure join systems concepts, multiple approaches, modelling, intervention, engagement and reflexive professional practice.
practice_connections: work with at least several approaches and know their limits
choose scope, scale and participation explicitly
learn from the consequences of intervention
common_misreadings: that systems practice is simply systems mapping
that the practitioner can remain outside the situation
that more tools create better judgement
that professionalisation removes contest and uncertainty
open_checks: connect capability statements to documented cases and failure modes
compare professional standards with practitioner-defined accounts of good work
profile.editorial_note: A developed working distinction for this release. The term remains contested and should be tested against rival usage and practice.

sources.notes: Primary public account by Beverly and Etienne Wenger-Trayner of systems convening as social-learning leadership across boundaries. Their FAQ explicitly says the work did not spring from systems theory.

sources.title: The Systemic Intervention Approach
sources.notes: Gerald Midgley's account of systemic intervention: boundary critique, values, marginalisation and methodological pluralism are central to the approach.

sources.title: Critical Systems Thinking: A Practitioner's Guide

sources.title: Opening the Box: Systems Thinking for Transformative Conversations
sources.notes: SCiO page for a short dialogical introduction to four layers of systems thinking: parts and wholes, nascent development, coherence and metamorphosis.

sources.title: Dancing With Systems
sources.notes: The Donella Meadows Project publishes the essay and its practical disciplines for acting with feedback-rich, nonlinear and partly unpredictable systems.

sources.title: The Hidden Power of Systems Thinking: Governance in a Climate Emergency
sources.notes: Routledge's page records Ray Ison and Ed Straw as authors and describes the book's focus on systems thinking, systemic governing and institutional change in the climate emergency.

sources.title: The Organic Systems Framework
sources.notes: Triarchy Press describes Barry Oshry's Organic Systems Framework as a pattern language for whole-system relationships and processes, including differentiation, integration, individuation and homogenisation.

sources.title: Barry Oshry — author profile
sources.notes: Triarchy Press describes Oshry's work on human systems, system-blindness and system-sight and lists his principal programmes and publications.

sources.title: Systems Thinking, Systems Practice — Wiley publisher page
sources.notes: The publisher describes the book as the culmination of action research using systems ideas in ill-structured real-world situations and records the 30-year retrospective edition.

sources.title: Cynefin — Cynefin.io
sources.notes: First-party maintained account of Cynefin as a decision-support framework based on bounded applicability, its domains, dynamics and development. Appropriate for the framework's own definitions; pair with the named papers for historical and scholarly claims.

sources.title: A Leader's Framework for Decision Making
sources.notes: Harvard Business Review record for the article by David J. Snowden and Mary E. Boone. It is a widely circulated practice-facing account of Cynefin; use it alongside earlier and later framework sources rather than as the entire theory.

sources.title: SenseMaker — The Cynefin Company
sources.notes: Canonical first-party description of SenseMaker and its use of self-interpreted micro-narratives. Use project reports and independent evaluations for claims about results in particular settings.
